sentences.en: It has been called the Holy Grail of modern biology.
sentences.zh: 它被称为现代生物学的圣杯。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: Costing more than £2 billion, it is the most ambitious scientific project since the Apollo programme that landed a man on the moon.
sentences.zh: 花费超过20亿英镑, 这是自阿波罗计划以来最雄心勃勃的科学项目, 使一个人登月。

grammar.type: 状语从句 + 分词结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作。

sentences.en: And it will take longer to accomplish than the lunar missions, for it will not be complete until early next century.
sentences.zh: 完成月球任务需要比月球任务更长时间,因为要到下个世纪初才能完成。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: Even before it is finished, according to those involved, this project should open up new understanding of, and new treatments for, many of the ailments that afflict humanity.
sentences.zh: 甚至在项目完成之前,根据所涉人员的说法,该项目应该使人们对影响人类的许多疾病有新的了解和新的治疗方法。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 分词结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作。

sentences.en: As a result of the Human Genome Project, there will be new hope of liberation from the shadows of cancer, heart disease, auto-immune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis, and some psychiatric illnesses.
sentences.zh: 由于人类基因组项目,将出现新的希望,希望摆脱癌症、心脏病、风湿性关节炎等自动免疫疾病以及一些精神病的阴影。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: The objective of the Human Genome Project is simple to state, but audacious in scope: to map and analyse every single gene within the double helix of humanity’s DNA.
sentences.zh: 人类基因组项目的目标简单易言,但范围大胆:绘制和分析人类DNA双螺旋内的每一基因。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: The project will reveal a new human anatomy — not the bones, muscles and sinews, but the complete genetic blueprint for a human being.
sentences.zh: 该项目将揭示一种新的人类解剖学——不是骨头、肌肉和绳索,而是人类的完整的基因蓝图。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Those working on the Human Genome Project claim that the new genetical anatomy will transform medicine and reduce human suffering in the twenty-first century.
sentences.zh: 人类基因组项目的工作人员声称,新的基因解剖学将在二十一世纪改变医学,减少人类痛苦。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: But others see the future through a darker glass, and fear that the project may open the door to a world peopled by Frankenstein’s monsters and disfigured by a new eugenics.
sentences.zh: 但其他人则透过更暗的玻璃来看待未来, 担心计划可能会为世界打开大门,

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: The genetic inheritance a baby receives from its parents at the moment of conception fixes much of its later development, determining characteristics as varied as whether it will have blue eyes or suffer from a lifethreatening illness such as cystic fibrosis.
sentences.zh: 婴儿在受孕时从父母那里得到的遗传遗产,决定了婴儿后期发育的大部分,确定各种特征,例如婴儿是蓝眼睛还是患有囊肿纤维化等危及生命的疾病。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作。

sentences.en: The human genome is the compendium of all these inherited genetic instructions.
sentences.zh: 人类基因组是所有这些遗传遗传指示的简编。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Written out along the double helix of DNA are the chemical letters of the genetic text.
sentences.zh: 沿着DNA双螺旋写出是遗传文本的化学字母

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: It is an extremely long text, for the human genome contains more than 3 billion letters:
sentences.zh: 人类基因组包含超过30亿个字母:

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: On the printed page it would fill about 7,000 volumes.
sentences.zh: 印刷页上将填充大约7 000卷。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Yet, within little more than a decade, the position of every letter and its relation to its neighbours will have been tracked down, analysed and recorded.
sentences.zh: 然而,在不到10年的时间里,将追踪、分析和记录每封信的立场及其与邻国的关系。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: Considering how many letters there are in the human genome, nature is an excellent proof-reader.
sentences.zh: 考虑到人类基因组中有多少字母,大自然是一个出色的校对者。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作。

sentences.en: But sometimes there are mistakes.
sentences.zh: 但有时也有错误

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: An error in a single ‘word’ — a gene — can give rise to the crippling condition of cystic fibrosis, the commonest genetic disorder among Caucasians.
sentences.zh: 单个词(一个基因)的错误可能导致细胞纤维化这一高加索人最常见的遗传疾病,其瘫痪状态。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: Errors in the genetic recipe for hemoglobin, the protein that gives blood its characteristic red colour and which carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body, give rise to the most common single-gene disorder in the world: thalassemia.
sentences.zh: 血红蛋白的遗传配方有误,蛋白质使血液具有其特有的红色,并将氧从肺部运到身体其他部位,因此导致世界上最常见的单一基因疾病:地中海贫血。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: More than 4,000 such single-gene defects are known to afflict humanity.
sentences.zh: 已知有4,000多种这种单一基因缺陷会影响人类。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: The majority of them are fatal; the majority of the victims are children.
sentences.zh: 其中大多数是致命的;大多数受害者是儿童。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: None of the single-gene disorders is a disease in the conventional sense, for which it would be possible to administer a curative drug: the defect is pre-programmed into every cell of the sufferer’s body.
sentences.zh: 单一基因疾病没有一个是传统意义上的疾病,因此可以使用治疗药物:缺陷预先排入患者身体的每一个细胞。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: But there is hope of progress.
sentences.zh: 但是,进展的希望仍然存在。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: In 1986, American researchers identified the genetic defect underlying one type of muscular dystrophy.
sentences.zh: 1986年,美国研究人员查明了一种肌肉萎缩背后的遗传缺陷。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: In 1989, a team of American and Canadian biologists announced that they had found the site of the gene which, when defective, gives rise to cystic fibrosis.
sentences.zh: 1989年,美国和加拿大生物学家小组宣布,他们找到了基因的所在地,当基因有缺陷时,基因会产生细胞纤维化。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 状语从句
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: Indeed, not only had they located the gene, they had analysed the sequence of letters within it and had identified the mistake responsible for the condition.
sentences.zh: 事实上,他们不仅找到了基因,还分析了其中字母顺序,并查明了造成该病症的错误。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: At the least, these scientific advances may offer a way of screening parents who might be at risk of transmitting a single-gene defect to any children that they conceive.
sentences.zh: 至少,这些科学进步可以提供一种方法,对可能面临向任何儿童传播单一基因缺陷风险的父母进行筛查。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: Foetuses can be tested while in the womb, and if found free of the genetic defect, the parents will be relieved of worry and stress, knowing that they will be delivered of a baby free from the disorder.
sentences.zh: 胎儿在子宫里可以接受测试, 如果发现胎儿没有遗传缺陷, 父母就会放心和压力, 因为他们知道他们会被生下一个不受疾病影响的孩子。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 状语从句
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: In the mid-1980s, the idea gained currency within the scientific world that the techniques which were successfully deciphering disorder-related genes could be applied to a larger project if science can learn the genetic spelling of cystic fibrosis, why not attempt to find out how to spell ‘human’?
sentences.zh: 1980年代中期,这个想法在科学界中获得了流行,即如果科学能够学习细胞纤维化的基因拼写,那么成功破译与疾病有关的基因的技术可以应用到一个更大的项目中,为什么不尝试找出“人类”的拼写方式?

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 被动语态
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: Momentum quickly built up behind the Human Genome Project and its objective of ‘sequencing’ the entire genome – writing out all the letters in their correct order.
sentences.zh: 人类基因组计划及其“顺序”目标背后的动力迅速形成 — — 将所有字母都按正确的顺序写出来。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: But the consequences of the Human Genome Project go far beyond a narrow focus on disease.
sentences.zh: 但是人类基因组项目的后果远远超出了狭隘地关注疾病的范围。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Some of its supporters have made claims of great extravagance – that the Project will bring us to understand, at the most fundamental level, what it is to be human.
sentences.zh: 某些支持者声称,该项目非常奢侈,在最基本的层面,它将使我们了解人类是什么。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: Yet many people are concerned that such an emphasis on humanity’s genetic constitution may distort our sense of values, and lead us to forget that human life is more than just the expression of a genetic program written in the chemistry of DNA.
sentences.zh: 然而许多人担心,如此强调人类基因宪法可能会扭曲我们的价值观感,并使我们忘记,人的生命不仅仅是DNA化学中写成的基因计划的表达。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: If properly applied, the new knowledge generated by the Human Genome Project may free humanity from the terrible scourge of diverse diseases.
sentences.zh: 如果适当应用,人类基因组项目产生的新知识可以使人类摆脱各种疾病的可怕祸害。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: But if the new knowledge is not used wisely, it also holds the threat of creating new forms of discrimination and new methods of oppression.
sentences.zh: 但如果新知识没有得到明智利用,它也有可能产生新的歧视形式和新的压迫方法。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: Many characteristics, such as height and intelligence, result not from the action of genes alone, but from subtle interactions between genes and the environment.
sentences.zh: 许多特征,如身高和智力,并非仅仅由于基因的作用,而是由于基因与环境之间的微妙互动。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: What would be the implications if humanity were to understand, with precision, the genetic constitution which, given the same environment, will predispose one person towards a higher intelligence than another individual whose genes were differently shuffled?
sentences.zh: 如果人类精确地理解基因结构,那么,如果人类在同样的环境中将一个人比另一个基因被不同地打乱的人更倾向于向高智商的人,那将会产生什么影响?

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 状语从句
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: Once before in this century, the relentless curiosity of scientific researchers brought to light forces of nature in the power of the atom, the mastery of which has shaped the destiny of nations and overshadowed all our lives.
sentences.zh: 从前在本世纪,科学研究者的无情好奇使原子的力量暴露了自然的力量,原子的掌握决定了各国的命运,使我们一生蒙上了阴影。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: The Human Genome Project holds the promise that, ultimately, we may be able to alter our genetic inheritance if we so choose.
sentences.zh: 人类基因组项目有望最终改变遗传遗产,

grammar.type: 状语从句 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: But there is the central moral problem: how can we ensure that when we choose, we choose correctly?
sentences.zh: 但是,有一个核心的道德问题:我们如何确保当我们选择时,我们选择正确?

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: That such a potential is a promise and not a threat?
sentences.zh: 这样一种潜力是一种承诺,而不是威胁?

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: We need only look at the past to understand the danger.
sentences.zh: 我们只需要看过去,才能理解危险。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

items.prompt: The passage compares the Project in scale to the…………………
The possible completion date of the Project is……………..
To write out the human genome on paper would require………………………..books.
A genetic problem cannot be treated with drugs because strictly speaking it is not a…………………….
Research into genetic defects had its first success in the discovery of the cause of one form of……………….
The second success of research into genetic defects was to find the cause of……………..
The Project will provide a new understanding of major diseases.
All the components which make up DNA are to be recorded and studied.
The correct order and inter-relation of all genetic data in all DNA will be mapped.
Parents will no longer worry about giving birth to defective offspring.
Being ‘human’ may be defined solely in terms of describable physical data.
People may be discriminated against in new ways.
From past experience humans may not use this new knowledge wisely.
